scope: Owned TIA Portal V21 scratch (CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1): a binary tree of 1,000 FC types Tree_0000..Tree_0999, each calling its two children (heap order), created through library_create_type in 10 changes of 100 (15-92 s apply per change, growing with library size) and released through library_release_version in 10 changes of 100 (346-365 s apply each). library_query dependencies from the root Tree_0999 captured all 1,000 versions with the authored edges in the project library (140.5 s) and, after library_publish of the root with its closure into a new global library (103 s apply), in the global library (111.0 s). A fresh consumer scratch instantiated the root with its closure from the archived global library and compiled cleanly (118.8 s apply, 1,000 Tree blocks in the inventory). Peak Portal working set 4.8 GB.
limitations: Observed timings on one Windows host (PCNico); not cross-machine budgets.
One FC tree with two callees per node; FB, UDT and diamond-shaped sharing are not part of the graph.
Dependency closures are bounded at 1,000 versions: a 1,023-node tree released completely but reported scopeComplete=false at the closure query (run lb_572a17e7).

The run needed two fixes in its source commit: compact library journals with a 32 MiB bound and a 16 MiB prepare refusal (an earlier 1,000-node publish overflowed the 8 MiB journal after its native change), and counted surplus compiler success rows (1,000 success rows exceeded the 500-row budget).

steps: project library closure of the root
global library closure of the root
